title: Unique extension of a bilinear functor to raw scalar localizations

from.place: The rational tensor construction extends the integral bilinear morphism map and proves the identity, composition and uniqueness laws.

statement: Let A be a commutative ring, p an element of A, and D an A-linear preadditive category [def-weil-linear-category]. Let B: D x D -> D be a functor, and let beta_{M,Mprime,N,Nprime}: Hom(M,Mprime) -> Hom(N,Nprime) -> Hom(B(M,N),B(Mprime,Nprime)) be A-linear separately and equal to B.map(a,b) on every pair of arrows. On the raw scalar localization D[1/p] [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] there is a unique functor F: D[1/p] x D[1/p] -> D[1/p] with F(M,N)=B(M,N) on the unchanged objects, separately A[1/p]-linear arrow maps, and action beta_p(c tensor a,d tensor b)=(cd) tensor B.map(a,b). Pure tensors use the scalar-first coordinates of [def-weil-module-base-change]. The arrow formula is interpreted by HEq when the prescribed object formulas are propositional equalities. No monoidal structure on B, flatness hypothesis or nonzeroness of A[1/p] is required.

source.place: Module tensor products and extension of scalars (Tags 00CV and 00CX); the assigned rational tensor paragraph of def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom. Generic categorical construction and induction proof written by G2.

proof.text: Lift beta to an A-linear map on the tensor product of the two integral Hom spaces. Base change to A[1/p], precompose with the inverse distribBaseChange equivalence and curry. On two pure tensors this explicitly gives (cd) tensor B.map(a,b), and its output object is the original B output.

Prove composition by induction on the four tensor-valued input arrows. The zero and sum cases follow from linearity of the extended arrow map and scalar-localized composition. For four pure tensors, the integral functor composition law identifies the arrow part and commutativity gives (x*xprime)*(y*yprime)=(xprime*yprime)*(x*y). The identity formula follows from B.map_id with coefficients one. Assemble these maps as a functor.

For a competing functor, use functor extensionality with its prescribed output-object equalities. Write its arrow action as the given bilinear map. Two tensor inductions prove the transported arrow equality: zeros and sums use preadditivity, and the pure-tensor case is exactly the specified HEq formula combined with the constructed generator equation. Hence the functors coincide, proving uniqueness.

The parent has a private Hom localization construction with an opposite first input. This new theorem extracts the covariant construction proved for this item, without any new sorry.

lean.statement:
theorem bilinearFunctor_existsUnique :
    ∃! F : ScalarLocalization A D p × ScalarLocalization A D p ⥤ ScalarLocalization A D p,
      (∀ MN, F.obj MN = ⟨B.obj (MN.1.obj, MN.2.obj)⟩) ∧
      (∀ M M' N N' : ScalarLocalization A D p,
        ∃ b : (M ⟶ M') →ₗ[Localization.Away p] (N ⟶ N') →ₗ[Localization.Away p]
            (F.obj (M, N) ⟶ F.obj (M', N')),
          (∀ a b', F.map (Prod.mkHom a b') = b a b') ∧
          ∀ (a : M.obj ⟶ M'.obj) (b' : N.obj ⟶ N'.obj) (c d : Localization.Away p),
            HEq (b (c ⊗ₜ[A] a) (d ⊗ₜ[A] b'))
              ((c * d) ⊗ₜ[A] B.map (Prod.mkHom a b')))
